title.en: Describe twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre cables
Compare their cost, bandwidth and noise immunity

say.en: Under the roads of every city lie copper wires and thin glass threads carrying our calls and videos. Why use glass when copper has worked for a century? In this lesson: Describe twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre cables.
Compare their cost, bandwidth and noise immunity.

body.en: A *twisted pair* cable has pairs of insulated copper wires twisted together; twisting reduces electromagnetic interference. It comes as unshielded (UTP) and shielded (STP) and is used in telephone lines and Ethernet LANs. A coaxial cable has a central copper conductor, an insulating layer, a braided metal shield and an outer cover; the shield reduces interference, so it carries higher frequencies and is used for cable TV.

points.en: *Twisted pair*: UTP and STP; cheap; LAN and telephone
*Coaxial*: copper core + insulation + braided shield; cable TV

narration.en: Twisted pair cables twist copper wires to cut noise and are used in LANs. Coaxial cables have a shielded copper core and are used for cable TV.

title.en: On the board: Inside three cables

say.en: A twisted pair has two insulated copper wires twisted together. Twisting cancels much of the electrical interference.
A coaxial cable has a copper core, insulation, a braided metal shield and an outer jacket. It is used for cable TV.
An optical fibre carries light. The core is surrounded by cladding with a lower refractive index.
Light hitting the boundary at a large angle is totally reflected, so it zigzags along the core even round bends.
Fibre has huge bandwidth, low loss and no electrical interference, but it is costly and fragile.

explanation.en: Twisting the pairs cuts interference cheaply; the coaxial shield allows higher frequencies for cable TV; optical fibre uses light, so it has huge bandwidth and no electrical interference, but costs more and is fragile.

body.en: An *optical fibre* carries data as pulses of light through a thin core of glass or plastic, surrounded by cladding of lower refractive index, so light is kept inside by total internal reflection. It offers very high bandwidth, low signal loss over long distances and immunity to electromagnetic interference. It is more expensive and fragile, and needs special skills to install. It is used for the backbones of telecom networks and the Internet.

narration.en: Optical fibre carries light through a glass core. It has huge bandwidth and ignores electrical noise, but it is costly and fragile.

problem.en: Choose a wired medium for: (i) a 20-computer college lab on a tight budget, (ii) cable TV in an apartment, (iii) a 40 km link between two city exchanges carrying thousands of calls.

steps.en: (i) Short distance, low cost → twisted pair (UTP) Ethernet cable.
(ii) TV signals need a shielded high-frequency cable → coaxial cable.
(iii) Long distance, very high bandwidth → optical fibre.
